payload.claim: The spatial, embodied, and fantastical cases show metaphors expanding 'what counts as the design space'—e.g., a room invites thresholds and guests, a status light invites ambient presence.

proposals.ref: link|https://doi.org/10.1145/3802974.3809449|question|what does a framing hide from view?|how does framing shape privacy reasoning?

payload.concept_name: What does a framing hide from view?
parent_path: How does framing shape privacy reasoning?
payload.claim: The relational case shows a companion metaphor making interpersonal norms feel applicable while hiding 'institutional actors, data movement, and power asymmetries,' leading youth to over-disclose.

proposals.ref: link|https://doi.org/10.1145/3802974.3809449|question|does changing the metaphor change actual disclosure?|

payload.concept_name: Does changing the metaphor change actual disclosure?
payload.claim: Names the empirical test the provocation invites: 'comparing identical privacy structures under different framings and tracing effects on actual disclosure.'

proposals.ref: link|http://arxiv.org/abs/2305.16589|value|wary of idealized assumptions|

payload.claim: The motivation section enacts wariness of idealized assumptions: a policy learned in an ideal nominal environment 'might fail catastrophically' under small deployment changes, so the work refuses to trust the nominal kernel.

proposals.ref: link|http://arxiv.org/abs/2305.16589|value|measured|

payload.claim: The results are stated with calibrated reach — 'near-optimal (up to log factors)', tight only when sigma ~ 1 and 'otherwise loose by at most a polynomial factor' — exemplifying disciplined, regime-scoped claiming rather than overclaiming.

proposals.ref: link|http://arxiv.org/abs/2305.16589|action|pin down the fundamental limit|

payload.claim: The paper establishes the first matching minimax upper (Theorem 1/3) and lower (Theorem 2/4) bounds for RMDP sample complexity, sandwiching the quantity to settle the intrinsic difficulty.

proposals.ref: link|http://arxiv.org/abs/2305.16589|action|construct a worst-case instance|pin down the fundamental limit

payload.claim: The lower bounds are proved by constructing two hard RMDP instances (M0, M1) inspired by the asymmetric structure of RMDPs, on which any estimator must err — a concrete worst-case construction.

proposals.ref: link|http://arxiv.org/abs/2305.16589|action|benchmark against an established method|pressure-test your own result

payload.claim: The central interpretation compares RMDP sample complexity directly against standard MDP complexity (SA/(1-gamma)^3 eps^2), concluding TV is never harder while chi-squared can be far harder.

proposals.ref: link|http://arxiv.org/abs/2305.16589|tool|simulator-based sampling|

payload.claim: The setup assumes a generative model drawing N i.i.d. samples per (s,a) from the nominal kernel, the instrument that isolates the statistical sample-complexity question.

proposals.ref: link|http://arxiv.org/abs/2305.16589|tool|worst-case uncertainty set|

payload.claim: Robustness is operationalized as a divergence ball U(P0) of radius sigma around the nominal kernel — specified via TV distance or chi-squared divergence — over which the worst-case value is optimized.

proposals.ref: link|http://arxiv.org/abs/2305.16589|question|what does robustness cost?|

payload.claim: The paper poses and answers exactly the cost-of-a-benefit question — 'is there a statistical premium one needs to pay in quest of additional robustness?' — showing the price depends on the uncertainty set's size and shape.

proposals.ref: link|https://doi.org/10.1140/epjc/s10052-026-15910-x|value|skeptical of one's own conclusions|rigor

payload.claim: The authors refuse to trust their novel ML-classifier limits alone, cross-checking them against an independent likelihood-ratio benchmark and against varied systematic assumptions.

proposals.ref: link|https://doi.org/10.1140/epjc/s10052-026-15910-x|value|measured|

payload.claim: Claims are deliberately bounded — spectral models are conservatively extended only to 10 TeV, and higher-confidence limits are flagged as less reliable rather than asserted.

proposals.ref: link|https://doi.org/10.1140/epjc/s10052-026-15910-x|value|forthcoming|

payload.claim: The paper volunteers a clear negative finding — that Asimov datasets cannot be reliably used with the ML classifiers — and openly notes the arbitrariness of its hyperparameter choices.

proposals.ref: link|https://doi.org/10.1140/epjc/s10052-026-15910-x|action|benchmark against an established method|pressure-test your own result

payload.claim: ALP exclusion regions are first derived with the standard likelihood-ratio test as a benchmark, then the new ML-classifier contours are overlaid and compared point by point.

proposals.ref: link|https://doi.org/10.1140/epjc/s10052-026-15910-x|action|test the result against alternative assumptions|pressure-test your own result

payload.concept_name: Test the result against alternative assumptions
payload.claim: Appendix D re-derives the 2σ sensitivity under halved/doubled energy binning, alternative magnetic-field parameters, and different EBL models to show the conclusions are robust.

proposals.ref: link|https://doi.org/10.1140/epjc/s10052-026-15910-x|action|simulate the null distribution rather than assume it|pressure-test your own result

payload.concept_name: Simulate the null distribution rather than assume it
payload.claim: Because Wilks' theorem cannot be applied to ALPs, the authors simulate 100/2000 datasets per parameter point to build the test-statistic distribution empirically instead of assuming its shape.

proposals.ref: link|https://doi.org/10.1140/epjc/s10052-026-15910-x|tool|machine-learning classifier|

payload.claim: An XGBoost classifier grid is trained on simulated spectra with and without ALP effects, learning which energy bins distinguish the two classes to constrain the parameter space.

proposals.ref: link|https://doi.org/10.1140/epjc/s10052-026-15910-x|question|can a learned classifier replace a hand-built test statistic?|

payload.concept_name: Can a learned classifier replace a hand-built test statistic?
payload.claim: The work directly tests whether ML classifiers yield exclusion regions consistent with the traditional likelihood-ratio test, finding them comparable at 2σ.

proposals.ref: link|https://doi.org/10.1140/epjc/s10052-026-15910-x|question|how far can a next-generation instrument push existing limits?|

payload.concept_name: How far can a next-generation instrument push existing limits?
payload.claim: Simulated CTAO observations of Mrk 501 and PKS 2155-304 project exclusion of a wide, previously unconstrained ALP mass range beyond current experimental limits.

proposals.ref: link|https://doi.org/10.1080/15592294.2026.2676911|value|measured|

payload.claim: Throughout, the authors hedge their central hypothesis and explicitly state its limits ('we do not claim genetic canalization', 'we do not expect a dog-specific epigenetic signature'), keeping claims proportionate to evidence.

proposals.ref: link|https://doi.org/10.1080/15592294.2026.2676911|value|skeptical of one's own conclusions|rigor

payload.claim: The authors specify a falsification criterion under which their own dog-linked account 'is weakened or rejected', exemplifying willingness to doubt the conclusion they advocate.

proposals.ref: link|https://doi.org/10.1080/15592294.2026.2676911|action|bound claims to what the evidence supports|

payload.concept_name: Bound claims to what the evidence supports
payload.claim: The Commentary carefully partitions within-lifetime plasticity, developmental programming, and transgenerational inheritance, asserting only the first two and explicitly disclaiming germline transmission.

proposals.ref: link|https://doi.org/10.1080/15592294.2026.2676911|action|build in ways the claim could fail|

payload.concept_name: Build in ways the claim could fail
payload.claim: The framework pre-specifies negative controls, within-site contrasts, a specificity test, competing explanations (diet, mobility, pathogen burden), and an explicit falsification criterion.

proposals.ref: link|https://doi.org/10.1080/15592294.2026.2676911|action|stage the test from a modern signal to deep time|

payload.concept_name: Stage the test from a modern signal to deep time
payload.claim: The authors design a two-stage path: first establish a reproducible methylation signal in modern dog-exposure cohorts, then use that baseline to motivate second-stage palaeoepigenetic comparisons.

proposals.ref: link|https://doi.org/10.1080/15592294.2026.2676911|question|what overlooked exposures shape human regulatory biology?|

payload.concept_name: What overlooked exposures shape human regulatory biology?
payload.claim: The introduction frames long-term human-dog co-residence as an 'under-recognised biological exposure' missing from human evolutionary science — naming an overlooked exposure axis.

proposals.ref: link|https://doi.org/10.1080/15592294.2026.2676911|question|can long-term relationships leave detectable molecular traces?|what overlooked exposures shape human regulatory biology?

parent_path: What overlooked exposures shape human regulatory biology?
payload.claim: The paper poses whether tens of millennia of dog cohabitation produced detectable context-linked epigenetic signatures recoverable from ancient and modern tissue.
